methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $15M total raised proxy.

private.name: Cobod
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series A)

data.narrative:
Material Evolution, a Series A housing and construction company founded by Liz Gilligan and Sam Clark, has raised $15M to date. The comparable universe is limited to one private peer (Cobod), with no applicable public comps in the frontier construction sector, constraining the depth of market-based validation available for this valuation.

Stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation approach given data constraints, anchors to the $15M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression. This yields an implied valuation of $30M. The method assumes normalized market conditions and conventional risk-adjustment patterns for the stage, though with only one private comparable and no public benchmarks, external calibration is limited.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M (low) to $34M (high), with a median of $30M. Key uncertainties include the lack of sector-specific public comps and limited private peer data, which restricts confidence in stage-based multiplier assumptions. The frontier construction market remains nascent and heterogeneous; progression multiples observed in adjacent sectors may not translate directly. Revenue traction, unit economics, and customer concentration—data not provided here—would materially inform the positioning within this range.
